question: What is the main goal of fluid and electrolyte regulation in the body?

options.A: Preventing the digestion of excess dietary proteins
options.B: Maintaining stable water volume and chemical composition
options.C: Slowing down cellular metabolism during resting states
options.D: Increasing the total amount of waste produced daily

explanation: The body keeps water and chemical levels within safe limits so that cells can work normally. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is understanding fluid balance especially important when caring for pregnant women?

options.A: Kidneys shut down entirely during the second trimester of gestation
options.B: Electrolyte levels never fluctuate at any point during normal gestation
options.C: Pregnancy causes massive shifts in maternal blood volume and fluid handling
options.D: Pregnant women completely stop losing water through normal respiration

explanation: Expectant mothers experience large changes in total body water, which makes them sensitive to fluid and electrolyte shifts. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which fluid compartment holds the largest percentage of total body water in an adult?
explanation: About two-thirds of total body water is stored inside the cells as intracellular fluid. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is the main electrolyte found inside body cells?
explanation: Potassium is the major positive ion found inside cells, while sodium is more common outside the cells. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the main working unit of the kidney that filters blood and makes urine?
explanation: The nephron is the microscopic unit in the kidney that handles filtering, reabsorbing, and making urine. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h3)

question: How do healthy kidneys respond when a person becomes very dehydrated?

options.A: They convert excess waste directly into solid mineral crystals
options.B: They produce a small volume of highly concentrated urine
options.C: They flush large amounts of water out through the bladder
options.D: They stop filtering blood entirely until fluid intake occurs

explanation: To save water when the body is dry, the kidneys reabsorb as much water as possible, making urine concentrated and small in volume. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which hormone helps the kidneys reabsorb water back into the body?
explanation: Antidiuretic hormone signals the kidney collecting ducts to let water pass back into the bloodstream, reducing urine output. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h4)

question: What triggers the adrenal glands to release aldosterone?

options.A: High blood volume stretching the heart muscle
options.B: Low blood pressure or low sodium levels
options.C: Excessive water intake during heavy exercise
options.D: Elevated blood sugar levels after a heavy meal

explanation: When blood pressure or sodium drops, the body releases aldosterone to help hold onto salt and water. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which electrolyte imbalance poses the most immediate danger to heart rhythm?
explanation: Potassium is vital for heart muscle stability, so abnormal levels can quickly disrupt heartbeats. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why are normal sodium levels so important for brain function?

options.A: Sodium acts as the primary energy source for brain cell mitochondria
options.B: Sodium shifts determine extracellular fluid volume and cellular osmolality
options.C: Sodium molecules form the structural scaffolding of neurons
options.D: Sodium directly prevents the buildup of urea inside brain tissue

explanation: Changes in blood sodium cause water to move in or out of brain cells, leading to swelling or shrinking that affects brain function. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the normal pH range for arterial blood in humans?
explanation: Normal arterial blood pH is kept strictly between 7.35 and 7.45 to keep body chemistry working properly. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h6)

question: How do the kidneys respond when a patient develops severe metabolic acidosis (too much acid)?

options.A: They excrete large amounts of bicarbonate into the urine and hold acid
options.B: They stop producing urine entirely to trap all acids in the tissues
options.C: They secrete more hydrogen ions into the urine and reabsorb bicarbonate
options.D: They rely exclusively on the lungs to fix the pH without renal changes

explanation: To fix acidosis, the kidneys pump extra acid into the urine while keeping bicarbonate in the blood to balance the pH. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h6)

question: A woman in her third trimester has mild ankle swelling after standing for a long time. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Complete absence of antidiuretic hormone secretion
options.B: Total renal failure caused by high dietary salt intake
options.C: Compression of pelvic veins by the enlarging uterus
options.D: Severe intracellular dehydration of all lower limb tissues

explanation: The heavy uterus presses on pelvic blood vessels, slowing blood return from the legs and causing normal ankle swelling. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a normal fluid change during the postpartum period?

options.A: Sweating or excessive sweating to shed fluid
options.C: Rapid diuresis of excess extracellular fluid volume
options.D: Permanent suppression of all kidney filtration

explanation: Kidney filtration does not shut down; postpartum fluid loss happens through heavy urination and sweating. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h7)
